title: feat: Dashboard design inconsistencies
description:
## What it solves Resolves: [part 2 of WA-2892](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2892/fix-design-inconsistencies) Design inconsistencies across the web app: network-logo badges looked different in every surface (borders vs none, different sizes, opaque `+N` bubbles), hover/selected states used opaque grays that broke on non-white surfaces and in dark mode, the safe-selector dropdown had no page dimming, and assorted spacing/radius drift in the sidebar, dashboard, and topbar. ## How this PR fixes it **Network-logo badges — one design everywhere** (reference: the safe-selector dropdown's `SafeRowStats`): - Logo separation is now a `mask-image` radial-gradient cutout instead of a painted border/ring — the gap is truly transparent, so it works on any background. Applied in `SafeRowStats` (inline) and in the shared `NetworkLogosList` stylesheet, where the geometry is driven by a `--network-logo-size` CSS variable so 18px/22px/24px stacks all get correct crescents. - The `+N` overflow indicator is transparent text (no more opaque `bg-muted` bubble) and sizes with the logos. - The accounts-table badge (`AccountItemChainBadge`) renders 22px logos capped at 3 + `+N`, matching the dropdown pill exactly (28px pill, 16px logo advance, 12.5→13px cut). **Adaptive tints instead of opaque grays:** - Row action icons (copy/explorer/rename) hover with `bg-foreground/5`; the pending-badge dot ring is `ring-white/50` — both composite correctly on any surface and in dark mode. - New theme token `background.lightHover` (`#E7FFF2` light / `#12FF801A` dark) for hovering the selected dropdown row; promoted into `@safe-global/theme` and generated into `vars.css`. - shadcn `--accent` aligned to the green accent scale (`#f0fdf4` / `#052e16`). **Safe-selector dropdown backdrop:** - Opening the dropdown dims the whole page (`SelectContent` gained an opt-in `showBackdrop` that renders base-ui's `Select.Backdrop` with the dialog-overlay styling). - The `SpaceSafeBar` pill and the popup stay lit: a second topbar-elevation tier (`useTopbarOverlayElevation`) dissolves the topbar's stacking context while open, and the bar lifts itself one step above the backdrop. - Dropdown balances render in primary color at 14px (was muted 12px). **Layout polish:** topbar gets 24px top padding; sidebar header spacing, switch-sidebar icon (`PanelRightIcon`), Safe logo radius, dashboard icon chips, and various spaces CSS fixes. ## How to test it 1. **Accounts table** (`/welcome/accounts` or spaces safe accounts): multi-chain rows show ≤3 stacked network logos with transparent gaps between them and a `+N` matching the pill background; hover a row — the pill tint follows. 2. **Safe-selector dropdown** (topbar): open it — page dims, the white SpaceSafeBar pill and the popup stay lit. The current safe's row is green; hovering it deepens the green (both themes). Row balances are 14px primary text. Network pills in rows match the accounts table. 3. **Row actions**: hover copy/explorer/rename icons on light and dark themes — subtle adaptive tint, no flat gray chips. 4. **Storybook**: `NetworkLogosList` → `InsideAccountBadgePill` story shows the badge configuration. ## Affected flows - Account list / accounts table browsing (network badges, workspace badges, row hover actions) - Safe switching via the topbar safe-selector dropdown (backdrop, selected-row highlight, balances) - Tx-flow / recovery topbar elevation (mechanism refactored, behavior unchanged) - Sidebar & dashboard visual polish (logo, header spacing, icon chips) ## Blast radius - `NetworkLogosList` (shared): consumers include address book tables, request-to-add, safe app preview drawer, new-safe review/overview, counterfactual success screen, SecurityHub table (18px logos) — all inherit the mask cutouts and transparent `+N`. - `RowIconAction` (shared): all AccountRow surfaces get the new hover tint. - `SelectContent` (`showBackdrop` opt-in): default unchanged — no other select gets a backdrop. - `useTopbarElevation`: refactored into a factory; existing `tx-flow`/`recovery` behavior preserved (covered by PageLayout tests). - `@safe-global/theme`: additive `background.lightHover` key — flows into generated Tamagui tokens; no mobile behavior change until used. - `--accent` change affects every shadcn component using accent (e.g. select/dropdown focus states) — now green-tinted instead of gray. ## Risks / not checked - Did not test on mobile app (theme key is additive only). - Storybook test-runner / Chromatic visual diffs not run locally — the intended diffs will appear on this PR and need accepting. - Mask cutouts skip chains whose logo fails to load (SVG fallback icon isn't masked) — same as before, no border either. - Wrapped logo rows (`flex-wrap` in `NetworkLogosList`) keep a masked right edge when a neighbor wraps to the next line — pre-existing rare case. - Backdrop layering verified on the topbar placement only; the safe selector is not rendered elsewhere today. ## Visual summary ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Before B1[Each surface: own borders,
sizes, opaque +N bubble] --> B2[Opaque grays break on
hover/dark surfaces] end subgraph After A0[SafeRowStats = reference design] --> A1[mask-image cutout
--network-logo-size var] A1 --> A2[NetworkLogosList
all badge surfaces] A0 --> A3[translucent tints:
bg-foreground/5, background.lightHover] end ``` ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph "Dropdown open — z-layers" Z1[page + sidebar + rest of header
dimmed under backdrop 1400] Z2[SpaceSafeBar pill — 1401

findings.claim: The stacked-logo crescent geometry is duplicated between an inline constant here and a CSS rule in NetworkLogosList's stylesheet, with comments in each referencing the other as the source of truth, creating a maintenance risk if one is changed without the other.

If the sticky `.topbarElevated` state and the overlay are ever active at the same time, the sticky positioning would create its own stacking context and could similarly defeat the intended z-index lift of the safe bar above the backdrop.
The new nested isCollapsed branch, which renders a centred size-10 logo tile, is not covered by tests, and the existing test file for this component was not updated.
Like the ReviewStep consumer, this component does not cap the logo list length, exposing the same wrap-related masking issue.

The global --accent token is changed app-wide from a neutral grey to green in both light and dark themes, but the change is only needed for the dashboard and header pills; every surface using focus:bg-accent or data-highlighted:bg-accent (Select, DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, Combobox items, and global search) will now highlight green, and --accent becomes identical to --sidebar-accent. This needs an explicit design decision, or the green should be scoped to a separate token rather than changing the shared one.
The component has no test file, so the new behavior where the menu anchors to the closest table row, falls back to the button, and hides the backdrop is untested.

The comment states the logo radius is 12px, but the actual logo size is 22px (making the radius 11px), so the comment is incorrect; if this duplication is addressed, the constant should also be replaced with a CSS-variable-driven class like the one used in NetworkLogosList and the radius comment corrected.

This consumer of the logo list does not cap the number of logos shown, which interacts with the wrap-related masking bug and can produce more uncovered crescent cutouts as more logos wrap onto new rows.

There is no test coverage for the new `useTopbarOverlayElevation` / `useIsTopbarAboveOverlay` hooks, and the existing test file only exercises the pre-existing modal elevation pair, not the new overlay pair.
The component uses the raw palette class text-green-500 instead of a theme token.

No test covers the new isDropdownActuallyOpen branches, including backdrop rendering only when showBackdrop is set and elevation triggering only when the dropdown is actually open; a regression in the disabled or !canOpen cases could leave the topbar elevated above a backdrop that isn't shown.

The shared shadcn `--accent` token was changed from a neutral color to green in both light mode (`#f5f5f5` to `#f0fdf4`) and dark mode (`#12ff8033` to `#052e16`) to restyle three Spaces surfaces, but this token is also used as the hover/focus background for every menu item across dropdown-menu, context-menu, select, combobox, and global search components, so every menu highlight app-wide turns green with nothing overriding it; if this is unintended it needs a scoped token instead, and if intended it should be called out in the PR description.
The `showBackdrop` behavior introduced alongside the overlay elevation changes has no test coverage.

The same crescent-mask geometry for stacked logos is duplicated: once as a hard-coded inline JS string of pixel values and once as a parameterised CSS rule that explicitly comments it replicates the JS version exactly, so if one is tuned the other will not follow; SafeRowStats could reuse the CSS-module class, or both could share a single helper.

The crescent mask rule targets `span:not(:last-child)`, but the `.networks` container uses `flex-wrap: wrap`, so the last logo on each wrapped row (not just the true last item) ends up with an uncovered crescent cutout since no neighbour logo overlaps it on that row.

The PR edits shared shadcn primitives, adding a showBackdrop prop to SelectContent and changing the SidebarTrigger icon and SidebarHeader padding/gap in sidebar.tsx, affecting every consumer of these components; it is unverified whether this was coordinated with the design-system rewrite or whether no such conflicting PR is open, since the PR description could not be checked.

The topbar wrapper's stacking context is removed via `.topbarAboveOverlay { z-index: auto }` so that the safe bar's elevated z-index can beat the dropdown backdrop, but the bar renders inside a `<header className="@container …">` element, and `container-type: inline-size` applies layout containment which always creates its own stacking context. As a result the bar's z-index only wins within the header, and the whole header still paints below the Select backdrop, so opening the safe-selector dropdown dims the entire topbar including the trigger, defeating the purpose of the elevation hooks.

Anchoring the context menu to `closest('tr')` and applying right alignment now applies to every consumer of this component, including non-table consumers such as SafeListItem, MultiAccountItem, and SafeCardReadOnly, which changes menu placement behavior for those cases even though a fallback prevents a crash.

No test verifies that the dropdown registers overlay elevation only when the dropdown is actually open, as opposed to when it is disabled or when `canOpen` is false; removing this registration line would not cause any test to fail, indicating a coverage gap.
The story decorator hard-codes the color value rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) instead of using a theme token.
Fallback SvgIcon logos that render without an `` element are never masked by the crescent-cutout styling, leaving them visually inconsistent with masked image logos.

The new useTopbarOverlayElevation and useIsTopbarAboveOverlay hooks and the createElevationHooks refactor have no tests; the existing test file was not updated to cover the overlay hooks, and the only reference is an unrelated jest mock. Missing coverage includes register/unregister behavior on open/close/unmount and verification that the two stores remain independent.
